lines: MeetingScribe turns your calls into notes and follow-ups.
No bot joins the meeting, and nothing leaves your computer unless you say so.
Join Teams, Zoom or Google Meet as usual. It records by itself, and a few minutes after you hang up, the note is ready.
A stand-up, a one-on-one and an incident review each get the note they need. You can add your own.
Every action item lands on one list, and work that keeps coming back shows as carried over.
Before your next call, a brief shows what was said last time and what is still open. It comes straight from your notes, so nothing is made up.
Send the recap and each person's follow-up to Slack, Teams, Gmail or Outlook. Nothing goes until you press the button.
Turn action items into Jira tickets, or hand one to an AI that opens a draft pull request.
Turn on MCP, and Claude or Cursor on your computer can read your meetings. It can only read.
Nobody on the call can see it, so telling them is up to you. It gives you a notice to paste into the chat.
List the meetings it must never record, and have old ones deleted automatically.
It is early software. The installers are unsigned, and a small local model can get details wrong, so read the note before you act on it.
It has only been tested on simulated calls, and the calendar, Slack and Teams only against stand-ins.
And recording people comes with legal rules, so ask first.
MeetingScribe. Meetings, written down and followed up.
